Primary antibody deficiency; recurrent respiratory and ear infections do not establish lasting organ damage.
Sickling hemoglobinopathy; retinopathy is a separately diagnosed complication. Other destructive organ complications are not consistently present in >=30%.
Intellectual disability and structural cranial abnormalities define the syndrome; reported bradycardia alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Marrow plasma-cell neoplasm; destructive bone disease affects most patients and direct paraprotein-related kidney injury occurs in roughly one-third or more.
Autoimmune necrotizing vasculitis; destructive skin lesions occur in most and peripheral neuropathy in roughly 30-60%. Background rheumatoid arthritis is separate.
Motor-neuron degeneration; denervation produces proximal muscle atrophy in 10/16 patients. Bulbar dysphagia does not establish gastrointestinal tissue damage.
Marfanoid skeletal development, advanced bone age and abdominal-wall hernia define the reported syndrome; no evidence supports additional damaged organs.
Familial panic disorder is psychiatric; hereditary neurological ancestry does not establish neurological organ damage.
Carcinoma of the reproductive ovary; familial occurrence does not establish endocrine dysfunction or another covered organ.
Organ-specific hereditary susceptibility to uveal melanoma; ocular labels the defining tumor site, without assuming an existing tumor or other organ damage.
Suppurative dental infection involving tissues around the tooth root; teeth and periodontal tissues belong to gastrointestinal.
Carcinoma arising in the adrenal medulla, an endocrine gland; no common additional organ damage is established.
Absent enteric ganglia cause severe intestinal dysmotility; the defined organ disorder is intestinal, without evidence of generalized neurological disease.
Epilepsy and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; congenital cardiac defects are occasional, below 30%.
Hereditary carcinoma of the reproductive prostate; no endocrine dysfunction or common direct damage to a covered organ is established.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; lasting pes cavus and hammertoe affect 4/5 patients, with frequent denervation-related muscle atrophy.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; atrial septal defect occurs in 3/10 patients, meeting the approximate 30% threshold. Other anomalies have limited denominators.
Initially steroid-sensitive idiopathic nephrotic syndrome is an immune-mediated podocytopathy. Hyperlipidemia is secondary; clinical thrombosis is very rare.
GNAO1-related epileptic encephalopathy with universal developmental impairment and seizures; reported structural abnormalities are cerebral.
Defined by speckled pigmentary nevi and cutaneous capillary malformations; common damaging ocular or neurological involvement is not established.
Inherited epilepsy with febrile and afebrile seizures; no evidence of common direct damage outside the nervous system.
Primary central nervous system melanoma located in the spinal cord; melanocytic histology does not imply skin involvement.
Cutaneous basal cell carcinoma with sebaceous differentiation; the tumor originates in skin.
Chylous collection in the testicular tunica vaginalis is a reproductive disorder; no endocrine dysfunction or infectious cause is established.
